content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli slaw salad is a fresh mix of thinly shredded broccoli, carrots, red cabbage and onion, tossed in a light vinaigrette made with oil, vinegar, mustard and honey. It offers a crisp texture, a mild bite and a subtle sweet note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli is rich in vitamins C, K and folate, as well as glucosinolates with antioxidant properties.
The term “slaw” comes from the English word for shredded cabbage, referring to finely sliced vegetables.
The salad is often served as a side to barbecue, fish or chicken because its bright flavor refreshes heavier dishes.
It can be prepared ahead of time – add the dressing just before serving to keep the vegetables crunchy.
Some recipes replace regular vinegar with rice or apple cider vinegar for a milder tang.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis, promoting healthy skin.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Fiber from broccoli and cabbage improves digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: The salad is low in calories, making it a great option for weight management.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Glucosinolates and carotenoids help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in broccoli contribute to normal blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy to cruciferous vegetables
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to broccoli or cabbage.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables can cause increased gas in sensitive people.

items.title: Possible pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic produce, rinse vegetables thoroughly to reduce residue.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish or side. Enhance it with nuts, pumpkin seeds, dried fruit, or toasted tofu for extra protein.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Store the dressing separately to maintain crunch.
